To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
homophilic adhesion between cadherin ectodomain fragments is mediated by two domains and that the binding of these fragments is not restricted to a single orientation.
cadherin domains bind in a modular manner and that cadherins can adhere in any one of three antiparallels alignments.
cadherin adhesions involve two domains, that the domains can be aligned in three ways, and that the interaction potentials are distance dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of homophilic adhesion.
the structural and functional basis of cell-cell adhesion.
the molecular mechanisms of homophilic adhesion and the role of domain organization in protein function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cadherin adhesiveness is not a simple matter.
the adhesion mechanism is a complex one involving the participation of several domains, and that the interaction potentials are distance-dependent.
homophilic adhesion between cadherin ectodomain is a result of multiple domains interactions, which are not unique to the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a novel mechanism of homophilic cell adhesion.
we have demonstrated that cadherin adhesions are not unique, but are instead similar to the interactions of other adhesion molecules.
we have shown that the interaction potentials of the cadherin ectodomain are not additive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structural basis of cadherin adhesiveness is more complex than previously thought.
cadherin domains are not simply structural elements that provide a framework for binding.
the interaction potentials between cadherns and other adhesion molecules can be quantified and that these potentials can be used to determine which domains are required to generate the interaction.
